Name: Bioregional Weaving Labs Collective / Ashoka
Agent notes for human: Added CATBIS: strong bioregional regeneration and European field-building relevance. Existing collaboration tag preserved; no new collaboration status inferred.
Description: Pan-European collective of 25+ system-changing organisations, funders, and impact investors initiated by Ashoka Netherlands and co-led by Commonland and OpEPA, with partners including the Presencing Institute and The Weaving Lab. Its mission is to mobilise 1 million changemakers to restore, protect, and regenerate 1 million hectares of land and sea in Europe by 2030. The core instrument is the Bioregional Weaving Lab (BWL) — a geographically grounded, multi-stakeholder partnership process that weaves together local innovators, farmers, policymakers, NGOs, and citizens around a shared vision for their territory. The process draws on Theory-U and the 4 Returns framework (natural, social, financial, and inspirational), helping communities map root causes, align on a holistic landscape plan, and connect with funders and investors at bioregional scale. To date, 8 BWLs have been established across Europe (Ireland, the Netherlands, and others), with a target of 10. The Collective represents hundreds of system changers working directly in bioregions on nature-based solutions, ecosystem restoration, and biodiversity.

Description: International organisation established by European States in 1993, headquartered in Joensuu, Finland, with offices in Barcelona, Bonn, Brussels, Rome, and Malaysia. Conducts interdisciplinary research and provides science-to-policy support on forest-related issues across three programmes: Bioeconomy, Governance, and Resilience. Also hosts the EFI Bioregions Facility, which supports bioregion-scale forest governance and landscape approaches across Europe. Strong overlap with the bioregional and Mediterranean ecosystem research agenda.

Description: Public research centre founded in 1987 by the Generalitat de Catalunya, UAB, and the Institut d'Estudis Catalans (IEC), with the UB and IRTA subsequently joining.
